subject: Media Literacy
title: Data Breaches and Their Consequences
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Data Breaches and Their Consequences.

hook.text: A data breach exposed 500 million hotel guests' passport numbers, addresses, and travel dates. Most never knew.

buildup.text: Data breaches occur when hackers or insiders access personal data stored by companies — often millions of records.

discovery.text: Breached data is sold on dark web markets — identities, passwords, financial details, and health records.

twist.text: Most companies collect far more data than they can secure. The data they don't need becomes the data that gets stolen.

climax.text: Every piece of data collected is a liability. The best protection is to never collect it in the first place.

punchline.text: They promised to protect your data. Then they lost it. To everyone.

quiz.question: What is the best protection against data breaches?
options: Companies not collecting more data than they can secure
